equations.latex: \frac{dM}{dt} = -\left[k_1(1 + k_4\max(a_0 - a_{ref}, 0)) + k_2 N + k_3 E\right] M
equations.explanation: Surviving motor neuron fraction M decays exponentially at a rate combining baseline degeneration (accelerated by age of onset), neuroinflammatory toxicity proportional to N, and EV-RNA burden E. The multiplicative M term ensures M remains in [0,1].

ALSFRS-R score F declines in proportion to the rate of motor neuron loss, scaled by k5, and partially recovers/compensates toward F_max at rate k6. This yields roughly 0.5-1.5 points/month decline in fast progressors. Compensation gated by surviving motor neuron fraction (audit revision).

equations.latex: \frac{dN}{dt} = k_7 (1 + k_9 E) \left(1 - M\right) - k_8 N
equations.explanation: Neuroinflammation index N is produced at a rate proportional to motor neuron loss (1-M) and enhanced by EV-RNA burden E, and cleared at rate k8. This creates a feedback loop where M loss drives N, which further accelerates M loss.

hazard_model.explanation: Mortality hazard increases when motor neuron fraction M falls below M_crit and when functional score F falls below F_crit. Survival probability S(t) = exp(-\int_0^t \lambda(s) ds). This links the ODE states to survival endpoints and allows fast vs slow progressor heterogeneity. Functional deficit normalized by F_crit so all terms share month^-1 units (audit revision).

model.heterogeneity: Per-patient parameters are sampled to produce fast vs slow progressors. Key varying parameters: k1 (0.004-0.030 month^-1), k2 (0.005-0.060 month^-1), k3 (0.000-0.050 month^-1), k4 (0.000-0.030 year^-1), k5 (20-60 points), k6 (0.000-0.150 month^-1), k7 (0.020-0.200 month^-1), k8 (0.030-0.250 month^-1), k9 (0.000-1.500), E (0.0-3.0), a0 (30-80 years), M_crit (0.10-0.35), F_crit (5-15 points), hM (0.020-0.200 month^-1), hF (0.010-0.150 month^-1). Fast progressors: high k1, k2, k3, k7, E, low k6, k8, high hM, hF. Slow progressors: opposite. This yields median survival from onset ranging from ~20 to ~48 months.
assumptions: The system is deterministic and well-mixed; spatial heterogeneity in motor neuron pools is neglected.
Motor neuron fraction M is normalized to 1 at symptom onset, though significant loss may have occurred pre-symptomatically.
ALSFRS-R decline is driven primarily by motor neuron loss, with a linear compensation term.
Neuroinflammation N is a lumped index representing microglial/astrocytic activation and peripheral immune signals.
EV-RNA burden E is constant per patient over the 60-month window, derived from baseline transcriptomic proxies.
Age of onset a0 accelerates baseline degeneration linearly above a reference age.
Mortality hazard depends only on current M and F, not on their rates of change.
No treatment effects are modeled; the system represents natural history.
literature_rationale: Motor neuron degeneration in ALS is progressive and approximately exponential in early stages [CITE-NEEDED: motor neuron loss kinetics in ALS].
Neuroinflammation contributes to motor neuron death via activated microglia and astrocytes [CITE-NEEDED: neuroinflammation in ALS pathogenesis].
Plasma GLAST+ sEV RNA cargo, including SRP72, NPY2R, and WDR36, may reflect loss of RNA-handling and neuroprotective functions [CITE-NEEDED: EV-RNA biomarkers in ALS].
ALSFRS-R declines at approximately 0.5-1.5 points/month in fast progressors [CITE-NEEDED: ALSFRS-R progression rates].
Median survival from onset in ALS is 20-48 months [CITE-NEEDED: ALS natural history survival].
Age of onset is a known prognostic factor, with older age associated with faster progression [CITE-NEEDED: age of onset effect on ALS progression].
Functional compensation by remaining motor units can partially mask motor neuron loss [CITE-NEEDED: motor unit compensation in ALS].
Survival hazard increases sharply when motor neuron reserve or functional score falls below critical thresholds [CITE-NEEDED: thresholds for mortality in ALS].
audit_revisions: Eq ALS-2 (functional decline): compensation term is now gated by surviving motor neuron fraction M so that F cannot recover toward F_max after severe motor neuron depletion: dF/dt = -k5(-dM/dt) + k6(F_max - F)M.

Hazard: the functional-deficit term now uses the normalized deficit (F_crit - F)/F_crit so hF carries consistent units of month^-1: lambda(t) = h0 + hM max(M_crit - M, 0) + hF max((F_crit - F)/F_crit, 0).
k5 is constrained to [10, 45] so that F_min = F_max - k5 lies below F_crit while F never becomes negative (F is clamped to [0, 48] in the simulator).
Neuroinflammation index N is bounded in the simulator (N <= 10) to prevent non-physiological explosion of the inflammation-driven death rate.
